title: Finite convolution: indices, contributions, and filters
convention: Each question states zero extension and the index origin. There is one correct option per question. Answer letters refer only to the order in this packet.

questions.prompt: A finite sequence is x = [3, −2, 4], with its first entry at index 0 and zero at every index outside the list. What is x[−1]?
Two lists have lengths 4 and 3. Both begin at index 0 and are zero elsewhere. Which index range is retained by their full linear convolution, including possible zero entries at the ends?
Let x = [2, −1, 3] and h = [0, 1]. Both lists begin at index 0 and are zero elsewhere. For y[n] = Σₖ x[k]h[n−k], what is the full output?
Let x = [2, −1, 3] and h = [1, 2], both starting at index 0 and zero elsewhere. For y[n] = Σₖ x[k]h[n−k], what is y[1]?
Let x = [2, −1, 3] and h = [1, 2], both starting at index 0 and zero elsewhere. Which list is the full linear convolution y[n] = Σₖ x[k]h[n−k]?
Let x = [1, 2] and h = [3, −1, 2], both starting at index 0 and zero elsewhere. At n = 2, which sum correctly computes y[2] = Σₖ x[k]h[2−k]?
An averaging kernel is h = [0.5, 0.5] and a finite input is x = [0, 4, 0]. Both start at index 0 and are zero elsewhere. What is their full linear convolution?
A first-difference kernel is h = [1, −1]. The finite input x = [2, 2, 2] begins at index 0 and is zero elsewhere. What is the full output y[n] = x[n] − x[n−1]?
An input list x = [1, 0, 0] and a kernel h = [2, −1] both begin at index 0 and are zero elsewhere. Which list retains the complete full linear convolution, including the declared trailing zeros?
For zero-extended lists indexed from 0, let x = [1, 2], z = [3, −1], and h = [1, 1]. Their full convolutions are x*h = [1, 3, 2] and z*h = [3, 2, −1]. What is (x+z)*h?
Let x = [1, 2] and h = [3, 4], both starting at 0 and zero elsewhere. Define convolution y[n] = Σₖ x[k]h[n−k], and define the real zero-lag correlation r[0] = Σₖ x[k]h[k]. What are y[0] and r[0]?
For finite lists indexed from 0 and zero elsewhere, x = [1, 0, 2] and h = [−1, 3] have full convolution x*h = [−1, 3, −2, 6]. What is the full convolution h*x?
